summary: This note is a short biography of Adolf Overweg, a member of a three-man British-backed expedition to central Africa in 1849-1851. The expedition, led first by James Richardson and then by Heinrich Barth, aimed to build British relations with central African kingdoms and explore unknown territory. Overweg's notable achievement was circumnavigating Lake Chad, and he died of an unknown illness in Maduari, Chad, after swimming in cold water.
one_line: Biography of Adolf Overweg, a German explorer on the 1850s British-backed Central African expedition who circumnavigated Lake Chad before dying in Chad.
key_facts: In 1849, Adolf Overweg joined a 3-man expedition under the command of James Richardson and Heinrich Barth.
Heinrich Barth later took command of the expedition after Richardson's death.
The expedition set to leave Tripoli in the Spring of 1850.
The expedition aimed to help the British government forge relations with central African kingdoms and explore unknown territory.
The expedition crossed the Sahara carrying a boat on the backs of camels.
In 1851 the expedition split up, with Adolf Overweg trekking by route of Zinder to Kukawa.
Overweg rejoined expedition scientist Heinrich Barth, who was then leader.
After 18 months of exploring the Adamawa Emirate and Benue River, Overweg completed his most notable feat of circumnavigating Lake Chad.
Adolf Overweg died of an unknown illness in Maduari, Chad.
Adolf Overweg died after swimming in cold waters.
